text:
rachel_support: heads-up  secret-scanner flagged a live payment-proxy API key in a support log bundle uploaded to internal-logs.sumo on 2026-03-25. The log contains 'PAYMENT_PROXY_KEY=pp_live_4a5b6c' in the request trace.

tom_payments: yikes. which environment? live key or staging?

rachel_support: it appears to be a live key — copied from a customer's debug dump pasted into our support ticket; the support engineer attached the raw trace file.

ian_sre: immediate risk: if any external systems had access to that Sumo dataset (partners, contractors, analytics), treat as potential exposure. Patch plan: 1) rotate the payment-proxy key 2) revoke access to the Sumo bundle 3) scan other support tickets for similar patterns 4) implement scrubbing for payment keys in uploads.

ops-bot: [automated] Created ticket S-5699: "Rotate exposed payment-proxy key + scrub logs" assigned to payments & support (P0). https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/S-5699

security-bot: [automated] Running targeted scan for regex '(pp_live_[A-Za-z0-9]{6,})' across internal-logs.sumo and support attachments. ETA ~20m.

luis_privacy: also flagging for PCI/PII review — any live payment keys in logs may have compliance implications. I'll join the ticket.

ian_sre: mitigation steps in chat (do now):
- tom_payments: rotate the exposed key and issue a replacement with reduced scopes (no refunds API)
- rachel_support: remove the raw log from Sumo and replace with sanitized excerpt; stop sharing full customer traces in tickets
- all: run `./tools/log-scan --pattern pp_live_ --path support/attachments` and quarantine matches

tom_payments: rotated key and limited new key scope to read-only transaction lookups; old key disabled. New key issued: pp_live_x9z8y7 (pushed to secrets manager). Updated ticket S-5699 with rotation timestamp.

rachel_support: removed the log bundle from Sumo and re-uploaded a redacted excerpt. Filed an internal note to remind support reps to scrub before attaching traces. PR to support playbook: https://github.com/redwood/support-playbooks/pull/77

security-bot: [automated] Quick scan results: 4 matches found across support attachments (internal-only forks). Creating follow-ups and assigning owners.

luis_privacy: confirming partner access list: analytics-team and vendor-telemetry had read access to the historic bucket. Please provide list of vendor IPs that pulled the object between 2026-03-20 and 2026-03-25.

ian_sre: collecting access logs, will attach to S-5699. Also recommending we add a content-moderation hook to the upload flow to redact patterns that look like payment keys or full PAN numbers.

tom_payments: checklist for product teams: rotate any keys with the pp_live_ prefix issued in March 2026, avoid storing live keys in debug dumps, prefer tokenized traces, and add automated redaction in support UI.

rachel_support: training note: adding mandatory step to use `support-redact` tool before attaching traces. Rolling training to on-call support this afternoon.

security-bot: [automated] Full sweep complete: 0 public exposures; 6 private artifacts flagged for manual review. See S-5699 for details.

luis_privacy: filing compliance note; will assess if this is reportable under PCI guidelines and update the ticket.

ian_sre: mitigation complete for now: key rotated, artifacts sanitized, scan jobs queued. Keeping S-5699 open for follow-ups and process changes.

rachel_support: closing Slack thread; follow-ups in S-5699. If you find other traces of payment keys DM @security and @privacy. :warning:
